name: Flock
description: Flock is a team communication platform with channels, messages, calls, files, applications, bots, webhooks, and the FlockOS developer platform.
agentUseSummary: Flock cannot currently be connected because an installed FlockOS app receives a persistent per-user token that acts on behalf of the user without granular read-only scopes. Bot and webhook integrations have different identities and authority, while publication for all Flock users requires provider involvement, so Relay requires an explicit product decision before defining actions.

blocked.label: Install a user-authorized app
blocked.description: Flock provides a persistent per-user installation token for API calls on behalf of the user without documented granular read-only scopes.

blocked.label: Use an app bot
blocked.description: A Flock bot has a different application identity and channel membership/posting boundary that requires separate product and safety rules.

blocked.label: Use incoming or outgoing webhooks
blocked.description: Customer-owned webhooks expose intentionally different message and event surfaces and are not interchangeable with a delegated user connection.

blocked.label: Publish Relay globally
blocked.description: Publication for every Flock user requires provider review and approval that this worker cannot obtain or assume.

blocked.label: Access Flock data
blocked.description: Users, teams, contacts, channels, chats, messages, files, calls, reminders, to-dos, integrations, broad history, raw methods, and every read or write remain unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent action can be enabled until Relay selects one exact Flock user, bot, or webhook authority model and obtains any required publication approval.

runtimeSupport.description: No Flock identity, authority, or wrapper contract is authorized to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No Flock identity, authority, or wrapper contract is authorized to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: FlockOS user installation provides broad per-user token authority without granular scopes; bot and webhook routes are different products, and global publication requires Flock involvement.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request credentials or show Connect. Reconsider after an explicit product/security decision selects a user-install, least-privilege bot, or narrow webhook model and any necessary Flock publication approval is obtained.

evidence.supports: Flock maintains a current platform for apps, messaging, bots, webhooks, methods, and events rather than a conventional OAuth provider surface.
FlockOS documents app install/uninstall events, persistent per-user tokens, signed event callbacks, and broad collaboration API methods without a granular read-only scope contract.
Flock operates an app store and developer route for installable applications, distinct from customer-owned webhook integrations.
Flock describes incoming webhooks, outgoing webhooks, custom apps, and an API as separate integration mechanisms.
